blocks.text: **Harshavardhana (606–647 CE)** of the **Pushyabhuti dynasty** made **Kanauj** the political centre of north India and was the **last great ancient Hindu emperor of the north**. His reign is richly documented by **Banabhatta's Harshacharita and the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)**.

rows: Defeated by the **Chalukya Pulakeshin II on the Narmada (c. 618-19 CE)** — could not expand into the Deccan.
A Shaiva who turned **Buddhist (Mahayana)**; held grand assemblies at **Kanauj & Prayag (every 5 years)**.
Wrote Sanskrit plays — **Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika**; patronised Nalanda.

items: **Hiuen-Tsang** (630–645 CE) visited **Harshavardhana**; his **Si-Yu-Ki** records Nalanda (10,000 students) & Harsha's welfare rule.

Harsha: last great northern emperor; defeated by **Pulakeshin II (Chalukya)** on the Narmada; convened the **Kannauj & Prayag assemblies**; author of **Ratnavali, Priyadarshika, Nagananda**; **Banabhatta** wrote Harshacharita.
Harsha stopped by Pulakeshin II at the Narmada; Banabhatta + Xuanzang are the sources; Kanauj & Prayag assemblies.
Harsha authored Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika — a scholar-king.

prelimsPointers: **Harshavardhana** — **Pushyabhuti/Vardhana** dynasty; capital moved to **Kanauj**.
Defeated by **Chalukya Pulakeshin II** on the **Narmada** (~618-19 CE).
**Banabhatta** (court poet) wrote **Harshacharita** & **Kadambari**.
**Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang)** visited; wrote **Si-Yu-Ki**; attended the Kanauj assembly.
Harsha held a grand assembly at **Prayag every 5 years** (charity/Kumbh-like).
Harsha authored the Sanskrit plays **Nagananda, Ratnavali, Priyadarshika**.
He patronised **Nalanda University** and Mahayana Buddhism.
**Hiuen-Tsang** = 'Prince of Pilgrims'; studied at Nalanda under **Silabhadra**.
Harsha's defeat by **Pulakeshin II** (Aihole inscription of Ravikirti records it).
mainsAngles: Assess Harsha's achievements and the sources for his reign.

glossary.definition: Banabhatta's Sanskrit biography of Harsha, a key source for his reign.
The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim (Hiuen Tsang) who visited Harsha's India and recorded it in Si-Yu-Ki.
The Vardhana dynasty of Thanesar/Kanauj to which Harsha belonged.

blocks.text: The **Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi) (6th–8th CE)** dominated the Deccan, most famously under **Pulakeshin II**, who checked Harsha. They pioneered the **Vesara temple style and rock-cut/structural temples at Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal** — 'the cradle of Indian temple architecture'.

rows: Greatest; defeated **Harsha** (Narmada); **Aihole inscription** by **Ravikirti**; received Persian embassy; defeated by Pallava **Narasimhavarman I** (Vatapi sacked).
**Vesara** style; **Aihole** ('cradle of Indian architecture'), **Pattadakal** (UNESCO), **Badami** cave temples.
Patronised **Hinduism, Jainism & Buddhism**; Vaishnava & Shaiva temples.

items: Pulakeshin II beat Harsha but was defeated by Pallava Narasimhavarman I (Vatapikonda).
Aihole = cradle of Indian temple architecture; Pattadakal = UNESCO; Vesara style.

prelimsPointers: Badami Chalukya capital — **Badami (Vatapi)**; founder **Pulakeshin I**.
**Pulakeshin II** — greatest; defeated **Harsha** on the Narmada.
**Aihole inscription** — by court poet **Ravikirti** (Jain), in Sanskrit.
Pallava **Narasimhavarman I ('Vatapikonda')** sacked Badami and killed Pulakeshin II.
Temple sites — **Aihole ('cradle of Indian temple architecture'), Pattadakal (UNESCO), Badami caves**.
Developed the **Vesara** (Deccan) temple style.
Chinese pilgrim **Xuanzang** visited the Chalukya kingdom.
mainsAngles: Discuss the contribution of the Badami Chalukyas to temple architecture.

glossary.definition: The Deccan temple style blending Nagara and Dravida features, developed by the Chalukyas.
Ravikirti's eulogy of Pulakeshin II, a key source recording his victory over Harsha.
The Badami Chalukya capital, sacked by the Pallava Narasimhavarman I.

blocks.text: The **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi (c. 624–1075 CE)**, founded by **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** (brother of Pulakeshin II), ruled **coastal Andhra for ~four centuries** and were pivotal for **Telugu literature** — patronising **Nannaya**, the Adikavi — before merging with the imperial Cholas.

rows: **Kubja Vishnuvardhana**, brother of Badami Chalukya **Pulakeshin II**; capital **Vengi**.
~400 years — the longest-ruling dynasty of coastal Andhra.
**Rajaraja Narendra** patronised **Nannaya (Adikavi)**, who began the **Telugu Mahabharatam**.
Merged with the **Cholas** via **Kulottunga I** (Chalukya-Chola line).

items: Kubja Vishnuvardhana (Pulakeshin II's brother) founded the Vengi line; capital Vengi.
Rajaraja Narendra → Nannaya → Telugu Mahabharatam is the key Telugu-literature fact.

prelimsPointers: **Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi** — founded by **Kubja Vishnuvardhana** (~624 CE), brother of Pulakeshin II.
Capital **Vengi**; ruled **coastal Andhra ~400 years**.
**Rajaraja Narendra** patronised **Nannaya**, the **Adikavi** (first Telugu poet).
Nannaya began the **Telugu Mahabharatam** (Andhra Mahabharatam).
The line later merged with the **Cholas** through **Kulottunga I**.
Bridged Deccan (Chalukya) and coastal-Andhra (Telugu) culture.
mainsAngles: Assess the Eastern Chalukyas' role in the growth of Telugu literature.

glossary.definition: The coastal-Andhra capital of the Eastern Chalukyas for some four centuries.
The 'Adikavi' (first poet) of Telugu, patronised by the Eastern Chalukya Rajaraja Narendra.

blocks.text: The **Rashtrakutas (753–982 CE)**, founded by **Dantidurga** with capital **Manyakheta**, were a great **western-Deccan imperial power** engaged in the **'tripartite struggle' for Kanauj**. They are immortalised by the **Kailasa temple at Ellora** and were patrons of **Kannada, Sanskrit and Jainism**.

rows: **Govinda III, Amoghavarsha I** (wrote **Kavirajamarga** in Kannada; **Ratnamalika**; Jain).
**Kailasa temple, Ellora** (rock-cut, Krishna I) — monolithic marvel; Elephanta caves influence.
Arab traveller **Al-Masudi**; praised as one of the four great empires of the world (Sulaiman).

items: Dantidurga founder; Amoghavarsha (Kavirajamarga, Kannada); Kailasa temple Ellora (Krishna I).

prelimsPointers: Rashtrakuta founder **Dantidurga**; capital **Manyakheta (Malkhed)**.
**Amoghavarsha I** — wrote **Kavirajamarga** (earliest Kannada poetics) & **Prashnottara Ratnamalika**; a Jain; called 'Ashoka of the South'.
**Kailasa temple at Ellora** — monolithic rock-cut, built by **Krishna I**.
**Tripartite struggle** for **Kanauj** — Rashtrakutas, Pratiharas, Palas.
**Govinda III** — greatest military conqueror.
Arab traveller **Al-Masudi** visited; Sulaiman ranked them among the world's great empires.
Patronised **Kannada & Sanskrit** literature and **Jainism**.
mainsAngles: Evaluate the Rashtrakutas' contribution to art and the tripartite struggle.

glossary.definition: The Rashtrakuta capital (modern Malkhed) in the western Deccan.
The earliest work on Kannada poetics, attributed to Amoghavarsha I.
The three-way contest among Rashtrakutas, Pratiharas and Palas for control of Kanauj.
